newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity finishes down in tandem with gas.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity finishes down in tandem with gas.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures finished lower in tandem with cheaper natural gas prices as well as lower Western spot electricity prices and mild weather, industry sources said.
"Loads are off with the weather, and gas prices were off today," said one futures trader.

January California Oregon Border (COB) futures finished down $2.04 at $23.75 after trades as low as $23.60 per megawatt hour (MWh), while February settled $1.09 lower at $18.71 after trade down to $18.50 per MWh.
Remaining COB deferreds finished down between five cents and $1.00.
January Palo Verde (PV) finished down $1.75 at $24.25 after trade as low as $23.85, while February PV ended $1.14 lower at $18.61 after trade down to $18.50 per MWh.
Remaining PV deferreds closed down between 15 and 50 cents.
Natural gas futures and physical gas finished significantly lower Monday, putting pressure on electricity prices, the sources said.
Downward pressure on electricity was also seen from lower electricity physicals prices and expectations of above-average hydroelectric availability in the Northwest in the new year.
Weather was expected to be mild through the West, with normal temperatures through the week in the Northwest and above normal temperatures forecast for the Southwest.
NYMEX said an estimated total of 510 COB and 222 PV contracts traded Monday.
